metadata.title: SAGA: A Fast Incremental Gradient Method With Support for Non-Strongly Convex Composite Objectives (Defazio, Bach, Lacoste-Julien, 2014)
metadata.framework: unbiased variance-reduced incremental gradient with proximal support
metadata.source_note: Extraction based on well-known content of arXiv:1407.0202.

nodes.name: Composite finite-sum optimization
nodes.statement: Minimize $P(w) = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n f_i(w) + h(w)$ where each $f_i$ is $L$-smooth (possibly non-convex), $h$ is a convex possibly non-smooth proximal-friendly regularizer (e.g., $\ell_1$ norm), and $P$ is optionally $\mu$-strongly convex.

nodes.name: SAGA gradient estimator
nodes.statement:
Maintain a table of stored gradients $\{\phi_i\}_{i=1}^n$, one per data point, initialized to $\phi_i^0 = 
abla f_i(w^0)$. At each step, sample $j \sim \mathrm{Uniform}(\{1,\ldots,n\})$ and use the SAGA estimator: $g_k = 
abla f_j(w_k) - \phi_j^k +  ar{\phi}^k$ where $ ar{\phi}^k =  rac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \phi_i^k$. Update the table: $\phi_j^{k+1} = 
abla f_j(w_k)$; all other $\phi_i^{k+1} = \phi_i^k$. This estimator is unbiased: $\mathbb{E}[g_k] = 
abla F(w_k)$ (where $F =  rac{1}{n}\sum f_i$).

nodes.name: SAGA update with proximal step
nodes.statement: The SAGA update: $w_{k+1} = \mathrm{prox}_{\eta h}(w_k - \eta g_k)$ where $\mathrm{prox}_{\eta h}(x) = \arg\min_z \{h(z) + \frac{1}{2\eta}\|z - x\|^2\}$. When $h = 0$, this reduces to $w_{k+1} = w_k - \eta g_k$.

nodes.name: Comparison with SAG and SVRG
nodes.statement: SAGA unifies SAG and SVRG: (1) SAG (Le Roux et al. 2012) uses the biased estimator $\bar{\phi}^k$ averaged from stored gradients; SAGA corrects this to an unbiased estimator by adding the current gradient correction $\nabla f_j(w_k) - \phi_j^k$. (2) SVRG (Johnson & Zhang 2013) requires periodic full gradient computations (epochs); SAGA updates incrementally with no epochs. SAGA's storage cost is $O(nd)$ (vs $O(d)$ for SVRG), but SAGA handles proximal terms naturally and avoids epoch boundaries.

nodes.name: Linear convergence of SAGA (strongly convex case)
nodes.statement: If each $f_i$ is $L$-smooth and $P$ is $\mu$-strongly convex with $\kappa = L/\mu$, SAGA with step size $\eta = 1/(2(\mu n + L))$ achieves: $\mathbb{E}[\|w_k - w^*\|^2] \le (1 - \min(1/(8\kappa), 1/(4n)))^k C_0$. The total complexity is $O((n + \kappa) \log(1/\epsilon))$, matching SVRG and SAG.
conclusions: Matches SAG and SVRG convergence rates

nodes.name: Convergence for non-strongly convex case
nodes.statement: When $P$ is convex but not strongly convex ($\mu = 0$), SAGA with step size $\eta = 1/(3L)$ achieves: $\mathbb{E}[P(w_k) - P(w^*)] = O(n/k + L\|w_0 - w^*\|^2/k)$, giving $O(n/\epsilon)$ complexity.
conclusions: $O(1/k)$ convergence rate for non-strongly convex objectives
